title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
title_zh: 面向机器人技术的Gym-Anything：用数字智能体扩展物理仿真

paragraphs.en: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. The core bottleneck is that creating better simulations requires significant expert effort and therefore does not scale. To address this, we introduce Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations. Our core insight is that simulation creation is a coding agent task, so improvements in coding agents translate directly into richer and more faithful simulations. We select simulations based on U.S. GDP data to cover economically valuable physical work, define what makes a good simulation and a good task, and develop an adversarial creation-audit loop that checks each simulation and task against these definitions. Using this pipeline, we build RoboWorld, a set of 25 simulations with 25 test and 175 training RL environments of varying difficulty. Even the best frontier models fail on every RoboWorld test task, achieving an average reward of only 0.06. Building on RoboWorld, we introduce several new ways for frontier models to improve, including in-context learning across repeated attempts, a privileged teacher that reads the simulator state and teaches a student in context, self-assisted learning from the model’s own privileged experience, and code policies that generate demonstrations across varied scenes to train vision-language-action models (VLAs) such as π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} . Each of these substantially improves performance. We release our pipeline, RL environments, and benchmark to facilitate future research. 1 1 1 Code and data are available at https://gym-anything.github.io/robotics .

paragraphs.en: Simulation is one of the most promising paths to training embodied AI at scale. Unlike the real world, a simulator can run thousands of episodes in parallel, reset instantly, expose the full ground-truth state, and provide rewards without human supervision ( Todorov et al., 2012 ; Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ; Tao et al., 2025 ) . For these advantages to matter, however, simulations must faithfully represent the real world. Although the field has developed various hand-built environments ( James et al., 2020 ; Yu et al., 2020 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2023 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) , a key bottleneck is that building additional, more realistic simulations requires significant time and expert effort. Indeed, despite decades of human progress, today’s simulations cover a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena (Tables 2 and 1 ), often with limited visual fidelity. Simulation as a path to embodied AI is hindered by the challenge of building diverse, realistic simulations at scale.
paragraphs.zh: 仿真是大规模训练具身智能最有前景的路径之一。 与真实世界不同，仿真器可以并行运行数千个回合（episode），即时重置，暴露完整的真实状态（ground-truth state），并在无需人工监督的情况下提供奖励（ Todorov et al., 2012 ; Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ; Tao et al., 2025 ）。 然而，要让这些优势发挥作用，仿真必须忠实地表征真实世界。 尽管该领域已经开发了各种手工构建的环境（ James et al., 2020 ; Yu et al., 2020 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2023 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ），但一个关键瓶颈在于，构建更多、更逼真的仿真需要大量的时间和专家投入。 的确，尽管人类已取得数十年的进展，如今的仿真仍只覆盖了狭窄范围的真实世界任务和物理现象（表 2 和表 1 ），且往往视觉保真度有限。 仿真作为通往具身智能的路径，受到大规模构建多样、逼真仿真这一挑战的阻碍。

paragraphs.en: Our core insight is that simulation creation can be framed as a coding agent task . Building a simulation means writing code, including assembling assets into scenes, configuring physics, defining tasks, and implementing rewards. Recently, coding agents have become increasingly capable of a wide range of coding-related work ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2024a ; Wang et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2024a ; Wang et al., 2024c ) . We hypothesize that frontier agents are already capable of building diverse robotics simulations with high visual fidelity and realistic physics. Moreover, framing simulation creation as a coding agent task allows future improvements in coding agents to translate into better simulations, thereby providing a means for scalable, realistic simulation creation that is expected to improve over time. Building on these insights, we introduce Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework in which coding agents create realistic robotics simulations of real-world physical work (Figure 2 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们的核心洞察是，仿真构建可以被界定为一项智能体编码任务。 构建仿真意味着编写代码，包括将资产组装进场景、配置物理特性、定义任务以及实现奖励。 近来，智能体在各类编码相关工作上的能力日益增强（Jimenez et al., 2024；Yang et al., 2024a；Wang et al., 2025a；Wang et al., 2024a；Wang et al., 2024c）。 我们假设，前沿智能体已经能够构建具有高视觉保真度和真实物理特性的多样化机器人仿真。 此外，将仿真构建界定为一项智能体编码任务，使智能体编码能力的未来提升能够转化为更好的仿真，从而提供一种可扩展的、真实的仿真构建方式，并且这种方式有望随时间不断改进。 基于这些洞察，我们推出 Gym-Anything for Robotics，这是一个由智能体构建真实世界物理工作的机器人仿真的框架（图 2）。

paragraphs.en: Building simulators for real physical work requires modeling a wide variety of materials and physical phenomena. For instance, a realistic titration requires the solution to form drops, mix, and turn pink rather than red at the endpoint. To organize the coverage of such phenomena in our simulation environments, we ground the selection of simulations in U.S. GDP data ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ; Patwardhan et al., 2025 ) . In brief, we consider each occupation, decompose the physical portion of the occupation’s tasks into atomic physical actions, and weight the actions by economic value. We then select simulations that cover the most valuable physical actions and any robotic and physics capabilities that these actions require. A coding agent then builds each simulation in code, assembles scenes from real assets, and configures the robot and physics (§3).
paragraphs.zh: 为真实的物理工作构建模拟器需要对各种各样的材料和物理现象进行建模。 例如，一个逼真的滴定实验要求溶液能够形成液滴、混合，并在滴定终点变为粉色而非红色。 为了组织我们的模拟环境对此类现象的覆盖，我们将模拟的选择建立在美国的 GDP 数据之上（Aggarwal et al., 2026；Patwardhan et al., 2025）。 简而言之，我们考虑每一种职业，将该职业任务的物理部分分解为原子级的物理动作，并根据经济价值为这些动作赋予权重。 然后，我们选择能够覆盖最有价值的物理动作以及这些动作所需的机器人和物理能力的模拟。 随后，一个编码智能体会用代码构建每个模拟，从真实资产组装场景，并配置机器人与物理引擎（§3）。

paragraphs.en: However, simulations built by coding agents frequently contain errors that make them unrealistic. For instance, a liquid simulation may not handle surface tension or inter-particle interactions correctly, or objects may pass through walls. Therefore, we develop an agentic creation-audit loop ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) for detecting issues in the simulations and fixing them. Specifically, we define criteria for what constitutes a good simulation, including realism, solvability, speed, and robustness to exploits, and then run a creation agent and four audit agents in an adversarial loop. The creation agent must produce evidence that its simulation is good, such as renders, physical measurements, and assisted demonstrations. The four audit agents, including an adversarial agent that tries to break the simulation, then check the evidence and report issues for the creation agent to fix.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，由智能体构建的仿真经常包含使其不真实的错误。 例如，流体仿真可能没有正确处理表面张力或粒子间相互作用，或者物体可能穿过墙壁。 因此，我们开发了一个智能体创建-审计循环（Aggarwal et al., 2026），用于检测仿真中的问题并加以修复。 具体而言，我们定义了构成良好仿真的标准，包括真实性、可解性、速度以及对漏洞利用的鲁棒性，然后在一个对抗性循环中运行一个创建智能体和四个审计智能体。 创建智能体必须提供证据证明其仿真是良好的，例如渲染结果、物理测量和辅助演示。 这四个审计智能体，包括一个试图破坏仿真的对抗性智能体，会检查这些证据并报告问题，供创建智能体修复。

paragraphs.en: Furthermore, for each simulation, we use coding agents to create multiple tasks and control their difficulty (§4). This is important since tasks that are all too easy or all too hard provide little signal for evaluating or improving models ( Shao et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ) . As with simulation creation, generated tasks may have issues such as being unsolvable or having incorrect rewards. We therefore define what makes a good task, and hand-curate checklists for six independent audit agents, which check each task against this definition, including solvability and reward correctness. We further ensure that each task’s reward measures both progress and the final outcome, computed from the physical state of the simulation. For instance, a cleanup task can credit each object placed in its correct location rather than only a fully cleaned scene. Finally, every task can be run with different robots, from single arms to bimanual arms and humanoids, and under variations of object poses, appearance, and physics, which change the scene but not the task itself.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，对于每次仿真，我们使用编码智能体创建多个任务并控制其难度（§4）。 这一点很重要，因为全过易或全过难的任务对评估或改进模型几乎没有信号（ Shao et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ）。 与仿真创建一样，生成的任务可能存在问题，例如无法求解或奖励不正确。 因此，我们定义了什么才算一个好任务，并手工整理了六个独立审计智能体的检查清单，它们根据该定义检查每个任务，包括可解性和奖励正确性。 我们进一步确保每个任务的奖励同时衡量进展和最终结果，这些奖励由仿真的物理状态计算得出。 例如，一个清理任务可以为每个被放到正确位置的物体给予奖励，而不是只在场景完全清理干净时才给予奖励。 最后，每个任务都可以用不同的机器人运行，从单臂到双臂和仿人机器人，并在物体位姿、外观和物理属性的变化下运行，这些变化会改变场景但不会改变任务本身。

sents.zh: 此外，对于每次仿真，我们使用编码智能体创建多个任务并控制其难度（§4）。

sents.zh: 这一点很重要，因为全过易或全过难的任务对评估或改进模型几乎没有信号（ Shao et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ）。

sents.en: As with simulation creation, generated tasks may have issues such as being unsolvable or having incorrect rewards.
sents.zh: 与仿真创建一样，生成的任务可能存在问题，例如无法求解或奖励不正确。

sents.en: We therefore define what makes a good task, and hand-curate checklists for six independent audit agents, which check each task against this definition, including solvability and reward correctness.
sents.zh: 因此，我们定义了什么才算一个好任务，并手工整理了六个独立审计智能体的检查清单，它们根据该定义检查每个任务，包括可解性和奖励正确性。

sents.en: We further ensure that each task’s reward measures both progress and the final outcome, computed from the physical state of the simulation.
sents.zh: 我们进一步确保每个任务的奖励同时衡量进展和最终结果，这些奖励由仿真的物理状态计算得出。

sents.en: For instance, a cleanup task can credit each object placed in its correct location rather than only a fully cleaned scene.
sents.zh: 例如，一个清理任务可以为每个被放到正确位置的物体给予奖励，而不是只在场景完全清理干净时才给予奖励。

sents.en: Finally, every task can be run with different robots, from single arms to bimanual arms and humanoids, and under variations of object poses, appearance, and physics, which change the scene but not the task itself.
sents.zh: 最后，每个任务都可以用不同的机器人运行，从单臂到双臂和仿人机器人，并在物体位姿、外观和物理属性的变化下运行，这些变化会改变场景但不会改变任务本身。

paragraphs.en: We use Gym-Anything for Robotics to construct RoboWorld, a collection of 25 simulations spanning domains such as manufacturing, construction, food service, laboratories, and logistics, with 25 test and 175 training RL environments of varying difficulty. RoboWorld is far from solved: even the best frontier models score 0% on the full benchmark, while on an easier subset, the best model reaches 32%. Beyond benchmarking, we introduce several new ways for models to learn on RoboWorld (§5). To do so, we exploit privileged access to the full ground-truth state, which is readily available in our simulations and a benefit of the simulation paradigm. We first show that models can improve on RoboWorld tasks through in-context learning, and that in-context learning is accelerated by access to the privileged simulation state. Since privileged state is unavailable at test time on a real robot, we develop three ways to leverage it as a learning signal, including (1) a teacher-student setup where the teacher has privileged access and teaches a student model through qualitative hints alone, (2) a “self-learning” setup where a model learns from its own privileged experience, and (3) a setup in which privileged code policies train the vision-language-action model (VLA) π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) , which observes only camera images and robot proprioception.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 Gym-Anything for Robotics 构建了 RoboWorld，这是一个包含 25 个模拟的集合，涵盖制造、建筑、餐饮服务、实验室和物流等领域，并提供了 25 个难度各异的测试强化学习环境和 175 个训练强化学习环境。 RoboWorld 远未被解决：即使是最好的前沿模型在完整基准上的得分也为 0%，而在一个较简单的子集上，最好的模型也仅达到 32%。 除了基准测试之外，我们还引入了几种让模型在 RoboWorld 上学习的新方法（§5）。 为此，我们利用了对完整真实状态的特权访问，这种访问在我们的模拟中 readily available，也是模拟范式的一大优势。 我们首先证明，模型可以通过上下文学习在 RoboWorld 任务上取得改进，并且访问特权模拟状态可以加速上下文学习。 由于在真实机器人上测试时无法获得特权状态，我们开发了三种将其作为学习信号的方法，包括：（1）师生设置，其中教师拥有特权访问，并仅通过定性提示来教导学生模型；（2）“自学习”设置，其中模型从自身的特权经验中学习；（3）一种由特权代码策略来训练视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA）π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) 的设置，该模型仅观察相机图像和机器人本体感觉。

paragraphs.en: In summary, we contribute (1) Gym-Anything for Robotics, a modular framework and multi-agent pipeline for automatically building high-quality robotics simulations, together with our definitions of what makes a good robotics simulation and a good task; (2) RoboWorld, 25 GDP-grounded simulations with 25 test and 175 training RL environments, each supporting swappable robots and variations of object poses, appearance, and physics; (3) an evaluation showing that frontier models perform poorly on RoboWorld, with no model scoring above 0% on the full benchmark; and (4) several new ways for models to learn in simulation, showing that frontier models improve through in-context learning and do so faster with privileged state, that a frontier model with privileged state can teach a student model without it, even through verbal hints, that a model can learn from its own privileged experience, and that code policies can train VLAs such as π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} .

paragraphs.en: In this section, we introduce the problem setup and the GDP-grounded selection of simulations. In § 3 , we describe our multi-agent strategy for creating simulations, and in § 4 , how we create tasks of controlled difficulty for each simulation.

paragraphs.en: We refer to a simulation E E as a scene implemented in code, consisting of objects with physical models (such as rigid, articulated, deformable, or liquid), a robot, cameras, and a physics engine that advances the physical state s s of the scene (Figure 3 ). Each simulation specifies a default robot, which can be swapped for other robots from a shared catalog, from single arms to bimanual arms and humanoids. Each simulation further supports variations of object poses, appearance, and physics, which change the scene in which a task is performed but not the task itself. For instance, our welding simulation is a robotic welding cell, in which a UR10e arm carrying a welding torch and an FR3 arm with a gripper work at a fixture table holding a steel plate and a bracket. Three cameras observe the cell, and the physics engine melts and solidifies the steel under the welding arc. The same cell can also be run with five other robot setups, from a single FR3 arm to a Unitree G1 humanoid, and its 10,000 variations shift the plate, change how far the wire sticks out of the torch, and add a draft that can blow the shielding gas away from the weld.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将仿真 E E 定义为以代码实现的场景，由具有物理模型的对象（如刚体、铰接体、可变形体或液体）、机器人、相机以及推进场景物理状态 s s 的物理引擎组成（图 3）。 每个仿真都指定一个默认机器人，该机器人可以从共享目录中替换为其他机器人，从单臂到双臂和人形机器人。 每个仿真还支持对象位姿、外观和物理特性的变化，这些变化会改变执行任务的场景，但不会改变任务本身。 例如，我们的焊接仿真是一个机器人焊接单元，其中一台携带焊枪的 UR10e 机械臂和一台带有夹爪的 FR3 机械臂在固定台上工作，固定台上放着一块钢板和一个支架。 三台相机观察该单元，物理引擎在焊接电弧下使钢材熔化并凝固。 同一个单元还可以用另外五种机器人配置运行，从单个 FR3 机械臂到 Unitree G1 人形机器人，其 10,000 个变体会移动钢板、改变焊丝伸出焊枪的长度，并加入可能将保护气体从焊缝处吹走气流的影响。

paragraphs.en: A task T = ( E s 0 , p , V ) T=(E_{s_{0}},p,V) consists of a simulation E E with initial state s 0 s_{0} , a natural-language instruction p p , and a verification function V V that maps the physical states of an episode to a binary success label and a reward r ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] r\in[0,1] . For instance, in one welding task, s 0 s_{0} has the bracket tacked to the plate, p p asks to “weld a continuous 1/4 in fillet along the near side in the horizontal position, end to end, and fill the crater,” and V V inspects the solidified weld under the AWS D1.1 welding code, checking that it is continuous and fused, reaches the specified size, and stays within the limits on undercut and porosity. If the weld fails, r r is proportional to the share of the required weld that is sound. Since swapping the robot or applying a variation changes only E E and s 0 s_{0} , this task can be run with any of the six robots and from any of the 10,000 variations.

paragraphs.en: Unlike the real world, a simulation can expose its full ground-truth state, such as object poses, contact forces, and material states. We therefore provide two levels of access to each simulation. Restricted access provides only what is available on a real robot: the task instruction, camera images, robot feedback, and documentation of the permitted robot commands. paragraphs.en: For robots trained in simulation to be broadly useful, simulations must cover the wide variety of physical work that people value, both in their jobs and in everyday life. Similar to prior work ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , we therefore ground our selection in public U.S. data (Figure 2 ), combining the tasks of each occupation ( Peterson et al., 2001 ) , the economic value of each occupation ( U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025b ; U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, 2025 ) , and the time people spend on everyday activities ( U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025a ) . However, what matters more than the tasks themselves are the atomic capabilities that they require, both from the simulation and from the robot. For instance, tightening a bolt requires a simulation that implements thread engagement and fastener friction, and a robot that can sense and limit torque. The same capabilities recur across many occupations and activities, so a simulation that provides them supports far more than a single task.

paragraphs.en: This leads to a simple question: which set of simulations provides the capabilities needed for the most valuable physical work? To answer it, we use an LLM to decompose each task into atomic physical actions, such as threading a bolt or pouring a liquid, and weight each action by the value of its task. We then group actions that a single simulation can reproduce, and identify the physics and robotic capabilities that each group requires. For instance, the action group tighten contains 529 actions from different tasks, including tightening bolts with a wrench, driving screws, and threading spark plugs. Finally, we select action groups with an optimization that maximizes the total value of actions whose required capabilities are all supplied by the selected simulations. To ensure diversity, we run this selection in tiers covering the economic core, strategically important and STEM domains, all 22 major occupation groups, niche occupations, underrepresented capabilities such as fluids and cloth, and everyday activities. Notably, we do not restrict the selection to what current simulators support, since coding agents implement the physics each action group requires (§ 3 ). In total, we select 120 action groups, each defining one simulation. In this work, we build 25 of them, and we continue to add more simulations on our project website. Appendix A describes the full pipeline.
paragraphs.zh: 这引出了一个简单的问题：哪一组仿真能够提供最有价值的实际工作所需的能力？ 为回答这个问题，我们使用一个LLM将每个任务分解为原子级的物理动作，例如给螺栓穿线或倾倒液体，并按其任务的价值为每个动作赋予权重。 然后，我们将单个仿真能够复现的动作归为一组，并确定每组所需的物理与机器人能力。 例如，动作组 tighten 包含来自不同任务的 529 个动作，包括用扳手拧紧螺栓、拧螺丝以及旋入火花塞。 最后，我们通过一种优化来选择动作组，使所需能力全部由所选仿真提供的动作的总价值最大化。 为确保多样性，我们分层次运行这一选择过程，涵盖经济核心领域、具有战略重要性和STEM的领域、全部 22 个主要职业大类、小众职业、代表性不足的能力（如流体和布料）以及日常活动。 值得注意的是，我们并不将选择范围局限于当前模拟器所支持的内容，因为编程智能体可以实现每个动作组所需的物理效果（§ 3 ）。 总计而言，我们选择了 120 个动作组，每组定义一个仿真。 在本工作中，我们构建了其中的 25 个，并将继续在项目网站上添加更多仿真。 附录 A 描述了完整的流程。

paragraphs.en: Building a realistic simulation is hard and laborious, even for experts ( Li et al., 2023 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024c ) . It requires researching how an activity is performed, assembling a scene from real assets, modeling the physics of the materials involved, and verifying that the result behaves physically. It often requires implementing physics that existing engines lack, such as cutting or chemical reactions. The key idea is that creating a simulation is itself a coding agent task. Building a simulation means writing code, and verifying it means running the simulation and measuring physical quantities, which coding agents can do. However, before building simulations at scale, we must define what we are building, i.e., what makes a good robotics simulation?
paragraphs.zh: 构建一个逼真的仿真是困难且费力的，即使是专家也不例外（Li et al., 2023; Nasiriany et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2024c）。 这需要研究某项活动是如何执行的、用真实资产组装场景、对所涉及材料的物理特性建模，并验证结果在物理上是合理的。 这通常需要实现现有引擎所缺乏的物理效果，例如切割或化学反应。 其关键思想是，创建仿真本身就是一项编码智能体任务。 构建仿真意味着编写代码，而验证仿真意味着运行仿真并测量物理量，这些编码智能体都能做到。 然而，在大规模构建仿真之前，我们必须定义我们要构建的是什么，即什么才是好的机器人仿真？

paragraphs.en: Realism. (a) The simulation is physically real to the degree that is required to represent a meaningful task. For instance, a titration simulation need not model every possible chemical reaction, but the solution must form drops, mix, and turn pink rather than red at the endpoint. (b) The scene looks real: ideally, a model shown a render and a real photograph cannot tell which one is real. (c) The scene and its tasks are relevant to the real-world activities of the action group. (d) Physical parameters, such as masses and friction coefficients, are grounded in digital evidence wherever such evidence exists.

paragraphs.en: Naively prompting even state-of-the-art coding agents results in simulations that fall short of these criteria. For instance, the agent may replace missing mechanics with animations or attachments, tune parameters until the behavior looks right, or report behavior that it never verified. Moreover, unlike software, where the application is real and a screenshot shows its true state, the physics of a simulation is written by the agent itself, so a render can show an object that has no physical effect. Similar to prior work ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , we therefore use a creation-audit loop (Figure 4 ). A creation agent receives a selected action group, researches how its activities are performed, designs a concrete scenario, and builds the simulation together with evidence that it meets each criterion, such as videos, physical measurements, and assisted demonstrations. Four independent audit agents, one per category, then check the simulation against the criteria above, including an adversarial agent that tries to break the simulation with legal robot actions, and report issues, which the creation agent fixes. We run three such rounds for every simulation, and all agents share a memory of lessons, so that each simulation benefits from earlier ones. In the instantiation of our pipeline described here, all agents are Claude Opus 5.5 ( Anthropic, 2025a ) , run via a coding agent harness such as Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025b ) . Appendix B provides further details.
paragraphs.zh: 即便是最先进的编码智能体，仅靠朴素的提示词得到的仿真也难以达到这些标准。 例如，智能体可能会用动画或附件来替代缺失的机制，不断调整参数直到行为看起来正确，或者报告它从未验证过的行为。 此外，与软件不同——软件的应用是真实的，截图能展示其真实状态——仿真的物理特性是由智能体自身编写的，因此渲染画面可能显示出一个没有任何物理效果的对象。 因此，与先前的工作（Aggarwal et al., 2026）类似，我们采用创建-审计循环（图 4）。 创建智能体接收一个选定的动作组，研究这些活动是如何进行的，设计一个具体的场景，并构建仿真，同时提供满足每条标准的证据，例如视频、物理测量和辅助演示。 随后，四个独立的审计智能体（每个类别一个）对照上述标准检查仿真，其中包括一个试图用合法的机器人动作破坏仿真的对抗性智能体，并报告问题，由创建智能体进行修复。 我们对每个仿真运行三轮这样的流程，并且所有智能体共享一个经验教训记忆，使每个仿真都能从先前的仿真中获益。 在此处描述的流水线实例化中，所有智能体均为 Claude Opus 5.5（Anthropic, 2025a），通过诸如 Claude Code（Anthropic, 2025b）等编码智能体框架运行。 附录 B 提供了更多细节。

sents.en: Naively prompting even state-of-the-art coding agents results in simulations that fall short of these criteria.
sents.zh: 即便是最先进的编码智能体，仅靠朴素的提示词得到的仿真也难以达到这些标准。

sents.en: For instance, the agent may replace missing mechanics with animations or attachments, tune parameters until the behavior looks right, or report behavior that it never verified.
sents.zh: 例如，智能体可能会用动画或附件来替代缺失的机制，不断调整参数直到行为看起来正确，或者报告它从未验证过的行为。

sents.en: Moreover, unlike software, where the application is real and a screenshot shows its true state, the physics of a simulation is written by the agent itself, so a render can show an object that has no physical effect.
sents.zh: 此外，与软件不同——软件的应用是真实的，截图能展示其真实状态——仿真的物理特性是由智能体自身编写的，因此渲染画面可能显示出一个没有任何物理效果的对象。

sents.en: Similar to prior work ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , we therefore use a creation-audit loop (Figure 4 ).
sents.zh: 因此，与先前的工作（Aggarwal et al., 2026）类似，我们采用创建-审计循环（图 4）。

sents.en: A creation agent receives a selected action group, researches how its activities are performed, designs a concrete scenario, and builds the simulation together with evidence that it meets each criterion, such as videos, physical measurements, and assisted demonstrations.
sents.zh: 创建智能体接收一个选定的动作组，研究这些活动是如何进行的，设计一个具体的场景，并构建仿真，同时提供满足每条标准的证据，例如视频、物理测量和辅助演示。

sents.en: Four independent audit agents, one per category, then check the simulation against the criteria above, including an adversarial agent that tries to break the simulation with legal robot actions, and report issues, which the creation agent fixes.
sents.zh: 随后，四个独立的审计智能体（每个类别一个）对照上述标准检查仿真，其中包括一个试图用合法的机器人动作破坏仿真的对抗性智能体，并报告问题，由创建智能体进行修复。

sents.en: We run three such rounds for every simulation, and all agents share a memory of lessons, so that each simulation benefits from earlier ones.
sents.zh: 我们对每个仿真运行三轮这样的流程，并且所有智能体共享一个经验教训记忆，使每个仿真都能从先前的仿真中获益。

sents.en: In the instantiation of our pipeline described here, all agents are Claude Opus 5.5 ( Anthropic, 2025a ) , run via a coding agent harness such as Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2025b ) .
sents.zh: 在此处描述的流水线实例化中，所有智能体均为 Claude Opus 5.5（Anthropic, 2025a），通过诸如 Claude Code（Anthropic, 2025b）等编码智能体框架运行。

paragraphs.en: Table 1 compares three RoboWorld simulations with the closest simulations in prior benchmarks, for liquids, chemistry, and cloth. In each domain, prior works rely on a general-purpose solver and report no quantitative check of the simulated physics, while we model the specific physics that each task depends on and verify it with physics checks (Table 1 ). For instance, in wine pouring, the bottle glugs because of the air trapped inside it, and its emptying rate matches a measured wine bottle ( Kenton et al., 2012 ) . In titration, each liquid particle carries its own chemical species, so pink appears where the titrant lands and fades as the flask is swirled. In laundry folding, garments are sewn from panels and held by the gripper only through friction. Appendix E extends this comparison to all 25 RoboWorld simulations.

paragraphs.en: Applying this pipeline to the action groups selected in § 2.2 , we construct 25 simulations spanning domains such as manufacturing, construction, food service, households, laboratories and healthcare, logistics, sports, and education, with physics including liquids, chemistry, cloth, molten metal, granular soil, pastes, soft tissue, and acoustics, and robots including single arms, bimanual arms, mobile manipulators, and humanoids.
paragraphs.zh: 将这一流程应用于 § 2.2 中选择的动作组，我们构建了 25 个仿真，涵盖制造、建筑、餐饮服务、家庭、实验室与医疗保健、物流、体育和教育等领域，涉及的物理现象包括液体、化学、布料、熔融金属、颗粒土壤、膏体、软组织和声学，涉及的机器人包括单臂、双臂、移动操作机器人和人形机器人。

paragraphs.en: For each simulation, we create multiple tasks. Recall from § 2.1 that a task consists of an initial state, a natural-language instruction, and a verification function. Once a simulation is built, creating a task reduces to writing these, together with any task-specific setup of the scene. For instance, a task in the wine-pouring simulation asks: “Pour a 150 mL glass of red wine from the bottle on the coaster into the Bordeaux glass at spot 2 (135-165 mL), without spilling or leaving drips running down the bottle, then stand the bottle back on its coaster and leave the glass upright on its spot.” Crucially, the physics of the simulation stays fixed, since a simulation should not change depending on whether a model can complete a task. As with simulations, we first ask: what makes a good task?
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个仿真，我们创建多个任务。 回顾 § 2.1，一个任务由初始状态、自然语言指令和验证函数组成。 一旦仿真构建完成，创建任务就只需编写这些内容，以及任何针对该任务的场景设置。 例如，倒酒仿真中的一个任务要求：“将一瓶红酒从杯垫上的瓶子里倒入 2 号位置（135-165 mL）的波尔多杯中 150 mL，不得洒出或让酒液沿着瓶身流下，然后将瓶子放回杯垫上，并让杯子正立于其位置上。”至关重要的是，仿真的物理特性保持固定，因为仿真不应随模型能否完成任务而改变。 与仿真一样，我们首先要问：什么样的任务才算好任务？

paragraphs.en: As with simulations, there is to our knowledge no established definition, so we define what a good task is through six criteria. A task must meet all six to be considered useful for evaluating and training robot policies:
paragraphs.zh: 与仿真一样，据我们所知尚无公认的定义，因此我们通过六条标准来定义什么是好的任务。 一个任务必须同时满足全部六条标准，才能被认为可用于评估和训练机器人策略：

sents.en: As with simulations, there is to our knowledge no established definition, so we define what a good task is through six criteria.
sents.zh: 与仿真一样，据我们所知尚无公认的定义，因此我们通过六条标准来定义什么是好的任务。

sents.en: A task must meet all six to be considered useful for evaluating and training robot policies:
sents.zh: 一个任务必须同时满足全部六条标准，才能被认为可用于评估和训练机器人策略：

paragraphs.en: Meaning. The task is a realistic and meaningful job, described naturally as one would describe it to a person, not as a checklist of verifier conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 语义。 该任务应是一份真实且有意义的_job_，以自然的方式向一个人描述，而不是以验证者条件的清单形式描述。

sents.en: Meaning.
sents.zh: 语义。

sents.en: The task is a realistic and meaningful job, described naturally as one would describe it to a person, not as a checklist of verifier conditions.
sents.zh: 该任务应是一份真实且有意义的_job_，以自然的方式向一个人描述，而不是以验证者条件的清单形式描述。

paragraphs.en: Setting. The scene, objects, and arrangement suit the specific task. For instance, a free kick that curls the ball requires a defensive wall, and a dribbling task requires cones.
paragraphs.zh: 场景设置。 场景、物体及其布置需符合特定任务的要求。 例如，需要让球弧线弯转的任意球任务需要人墙，而运球任务需要锥形标志桶。

sents.en: Setting.
sents.zh: 场景设置。

sents.en: The scene, objects, and arrangement suit the specific task.
sents.zh: 场景、物体及其布置需符合特定任务的要求。

sents.en: For instance, a free kick that curls the ball requires a defensive wall, and a dribbling task requires cones.

paragraphs.en: Verifier correctness. The verifier is deterministic and computed from the physical state of the simulation, without a VLM judge. It has neither false positives, such as accepting a cup placed over a ball for a task of putting the ball in the cup, nor false negatives, such as requiring the ball to rest at the exact center of the cup when the task did not ask for it.
paragraphs.zh: 验证器的正确性。 验证器是确定性的，并且根据仿真的物理状态计算得出，无需 VLM 裁判。 它既没有假阳性，例如在“把球放进杯子”的任务中接受了将杯子扣在球上的情况；也没有假阴性，例如在任务并未要求的情况下要求球必须停在杯子的正中心。

sents.en: Verifier correctness.
sents.zh: 验证器的正确性。

sents.en: It has neither false positives, such as accepting a cup placed over a ball for a task of putting the ball in the cup, nor false negatives, such as requiring the ball to rest at the exact center of the cup when the task did not ask for it.

sents.en: Solvability.
sents.zh: 可解性。

sents.en: As for simulations, assisted demonstrations show that every interaction that the task requires is physically achievable, without requiring an end-to-end solution.

paragraphs.en: Reward quality. The reward gives continuous partial credit that reflects meaningful progress, and full credit to every valid solution, irrespective of the strategy used. For instance, a cleanup task credits each object placed in its correct location.
paragraphs.zh: 奖励质量。 奖励应提供反映有意义进展的连续部分得分，并对每个有效解答给予满分，无论其采用何种策略。 例如，一个清理任务会为每个被放到正确位置的对象给予得分。

sents.zh: 奖励质量。

sents.zh: 奖励应提供反映有意义进展的连续部分得分，并对每个有效解答给予满分，无论其采用何种策略。

paragraphs.en: Difficulty coverage. Tasks that are all too easy or all too hard provide little signal for evaluating or improving models ( Shao et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ) . We therefore measure the difficulty of each task with a weaker and a stronger model, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5, and target a spread of success rates for both. This gives a ladder of difficulty that remains informative for both weaker and stronger models.
paragraphs.zh: 难度覆盖。 全部太简单或全部太困难的任务，对于评估或改进模型几乎没有信号（Shao et al., 2024；Yu et al., 2025）。 因此，我们用一个较弱的模型和一个较强的模型（Claude Haiku 5.5 和 Claude Opus 5.5）来测量每个任务的难度，并针对两者的成功率设定一个分布区间。 这就形成了一个难度阶梯，对较弱和较强的模型都保持信息量。

paragraphs.en: Similar to simulations, a task creation agent proposes tasks for each simulation, targeting five tasks per simulation that are diverse in the capabilities that they test, their difficulty, and the components of the simulation that they involve. Six independent audit agents, one per criterion, then check each task and report issues, which the task creation agent fixes, for at most three rounds. In addition, the agent uses recorded evaluation trajectories to create tasks of targeted difficulty. For instance, after observing a solver agent’s (in our instantiation, Claude Haiku’s) attempts at applying labels, the agent creates tasks targeting success rates of 100, 50, and 0%: repairing a single lifted label corner, repairing several lifted regions, and picking up a printed label and applying it around a curved specimen tube, respectively. See Appendix C for further details.

paragraphs.en: Consider the whiteboard simulation shown in Figure 5 . By default, a Unitree G1 humanoid stands about a meter from a classroom whiteboard, with six capped markers and a magnetic eraser in the tray. Its hardest task gives the robot a reference drawing and asks: “Copy the supplied colour-coded diagram of the Golden Gate Bridge onto the whiteboard, using the markers in the tray: orange towers, red cables and hangers, black roadway and blue water.” The verifier reads only the ink left on the board and scores the copy on fidelity, cleanliness, and placement: each of the 12 elements of the diagram, such as a tower or the roadway, must be at least 90% covered, at most 1 cm 2 of ink may lie elsewhere, and the copy must sit within 30 mm of where the reference shows it. The reward is computed from these three scores, so that, for instance, a copy with a missing cable still earns partial reward. Further, the same task can be easily varied and run with any of the six robot setups in Figure 5 , such as the H1-2 humanoid or a mobile base with two FR3 arms, and under variations that move the drawing, reorder the markers, and change the robot’s starting posture. paragraphs.en: Applying this pipeline to the simulations constructed in § 3 , we obtain RoboWorld, a collection of 200 RL environments across 25 simulations, 25 for testing and 175 for training, each with a deterministic verifier and a continuous reward. Each of the 200 environments supports swappable robots, from single arms to bimanual arms and humanoids, and variations of object poses, appearance, and physics. These variations are not considered to be separate tasks. Rather, they give many initial states of the same task, for training policies that generalize. We further take an easier subset of 25 tasks from the training split. Table 2 compares RoboWorld with existing robotics benchmarks. Several of them simulate liquids or cloth, are built by AI, or check their physics against real measurements, but RoboWorld is the only one that does all of these and also selects its simulations from job data. We release RoboWorld both as a benchmark and as RL environments for training.
paragraphs.zh: 将该流程应用于第 3 节中构建的仿真，我们得到了 RoboWorld，这是一组跨越 25 个仿真的 200 个强化学习环境，其中 25 个用于测试，175 个用于训练，每个环境都带有确定性验证器和连续奖励。 这 200 个环境中的每一个都支持可更换的机器人，从单臂到双臂和仿人机器人，并支持物体位姿、外观和物理属性的多种变化。 这些变化不被视为独立的任务。 相反，它们提供了同一任务的许多初始状态，用于训练能够泛化的策略。 我们进一步从训练集中选取了较简单的 25 个任务子集。 表 2 将 RoboWorld 与现有机器人学基准进行了比较。 其中一些基准模拟液体或布料、由 AI 构建、或用真实测量来检验其物理效果，但 RoboWorld 是唯一一个同时做到所有这些、并且还从工作数据中选取其仿真的基准。 我们同时以基准和用于训练的强化学习环境的形式发布 RoboWorld。

paragraphs.en: Realistic simulations open up a new way to learn physical skills: practicing in simulation, without the cost and risk of a real robot. Prior work mostly uses simulation to train small policies with reinforcement learning, often over millions of trials per task ( Tobin et al., 2017 ; Peng et al., 2018 ; Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ) . Frontier models can learn in a different way, since they can reason about a task, write code, and improve from feedback within a single context. We therefore study how frontier models can learn in simulation, and how what they learn can be passed to the models and policies that control a real robot.
paragraphs.zh: 逼真的仿真为学习物理技能开辟了一条新途径：在仿真中练习，而无需承担真实机器人的成本与风险。 以往的工作大多使用仿真配合强化学习来训练小型策略，每个任务往往需要数百万次尝试（Tobin et al., 2017；Peng et al., 2018；Makoviychuk et al., 2021）。 前沿模型可以用不同的方式学习，因为它们能够对任务进行推理、编写代码，并在单个上下文中根据反馈进行改进。 因此，我们研究前沿模型如何能在仿真中学习，以及它们所学到的内容如何能传递给控制真实机器人的模型和策略。

paragraphs.en: To do so, we use three features of simulation that the real world lacks: privileged access to the full ground-truth state, instant resets to the same initial state, and initial states that are easy to vary. We first study how frontier models improve on RoboWorld tasks through in-context learning, and how privileged state accelerates this improvement. Since privileged state is unavailable on a real robot, we then develop three ways to pass its benefits to models and policies that lack it: coaching through qualitative hints, learning from a model’s own privileged experience, and training VLAs from privileged code policies (Figure 2 ). In particular, since a simulation provides privileged state and can be run at scale, a frontier model can write code policies whose demonstrations train small policies that can be deployed on a real robot, raising the success of π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} from 0% to 53% (§ 6.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 为此，我们利用了仿真的三个现实世界所不具备的特性：对完整真值状态（ground-truth state）的特权访问、可即时重置到相同初始状态，以及易于变化的初始状态。 我们首先研究前沿模型如何通过上下文学习在 RoboWorld 任务上取得提升，以及特权状态如何加速这一提升。 由于特权状态在真实机器人上不可用，我们随后开发了三种方法，将其优势传递给不具备它的模型和策略：通过定性提示进行引导（coaching）、从模型自身的特权经验中学习，以及从特权代码策略训练 VLA（图 2）。 特别地，由于仿真提供特权状态且可以大规模运行，前沿模型可以编写代码策略，其演示数据可用于训练能够部署在真实机器人上的小型策略，从而将 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 的成功率从 0% 提升到 53%（§ 6.3）。

paragraphs.en: Since a simulation can be reset instantly, a frontier model can attempt the same task repeatedly and improve from its own failures within a single context, without any weight updates ( Brown et al., 2020 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . paragraphs.en: Since privileged state is unavailable outside simulation, we next study whether a model with privileged access can teach a student model that lacks it, similar to teacher-student training with privileged information in robot learning ( Chen et al., 2020 ; Lee et al., 2020 ) . First, a teacher model with privileged access attempts the task, without knowing that it will later teach. Once it finishes, we fork its conversation and workspace into a coach, so that the coach keeps what the teacher learned about the task. A fresh student model with restricted access then attempts the task under the same budget, and may ask the coach for at most ten hints. Before each reply, the coach reads the current privileged state of the student’s simulation, so it can see mistakes the student cannot observe. It then replies with a single qualitative hint about the student’s mistake or approach. Hints never contain positions, coordinates, or numerical robot commands, and the coach cannot act on the simulation, so the student must still act on its own observations. We compare coached students against solo students with the same model, budget, and initial states. In our experiments, Claude Opus 5.5 serves as both the teacher and the student.
paragraphs.zh: 由于特权状态在模拟之外不可用，我们接下来研究拥有特权访问的模型能否教授缺乏该访问的学生模型，这类似于机器人学习中利用特权信息的师生训练（Chen et al., 2020；Lee et al., 2020）。 首先，一个拥有特权访问的教师模型尝试该任务，但它并不知道之后要去教学。 教师完成后，我们将其对话和工作区分叉为一个教练，使教练保留教师对该任务所学到的内容。 随后，一个访问受限的全新学生智能体在相同预算下尝试该任务，并且最多可以向教练请求十条提示。 在每次回复之前，教练会读取学生模拟的当前特权状态，因此它能看到学生自己无法观察到的错误。 然后它以单条定性提示的形式回复学生的错误或做法。 提示绝不包含位置、坐标或数值化的机器人指令，且教练不能对模拟进行操作，因此学生仍必须依靠自己的观察来行动。 我们将受教练指导的学生智能体与具有相同模型、预算和初始状态的单独行动的学生智能体进行比较。 在我们的实验中，Claude Opus 5.5 同时担任教师和学生。

paragraphs.en: In all settings above, a frontier model controls the robot step by step, which is slow and costly. Simulation enables a different approach: a frontier model with privileged access writes a policy as code ( Liang et al., 2023 ) , and the demonstrations of this code policy train a small VLA that can be deployed on a real robot. A code policy is a Python program that reads camera images, robot state, and privileged task-object state, and outputs only ordinary robot commands, so it cannot move objects, apply forces, change physics, or reset the simulation. For instance, a code policy removes the lid of a gift box with two arms by reading object poses and contact forces, solving the inverse kinematics of the arms, and sending joint targets. Since a code policy runs without model calls, it can be run cheaply across thousands of varied initial states. We use its successful rollouts as demonstrations of camera images and robot state, and train π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) , a VLA that observes only three camera views and robot proprioception, without any object state.

paragraphs.en: To evaluate many kinds of policies, from frontier models to code policies and learned visuomotor policies, we build the Gym-Anything for Robotics library, which gives every simulation the same interface. As a result, any policy can run on any simulation without simulation-specific code. Behind this interface, each simulation can use its own physics engine and custom solvers, and its robot can be swapped for others, from single arms to bimanual arms and humanoids. The same simulation can also be run with restricted access, as on a real robot, or with privileged access to its full state (§ 2.1 ), so it serves evaluation, privileged experiments, and training alike. Appendix D provides further details.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估从前沿模型到代码策略和学习得到的视觉运动策略等多种策略，我们构建了 Gym-Anything for Robotics 库，它为每个仿真提供相同的接口。 因此，任何策略都可以在任何仿真上运行，而无需仿真特定的代码。 在该接口背后，每个仿真可以使用自己的物理引擎和自定义求解器，其机器人也可以替换为其他机器人，从单臂到双臂和人形机器人。 同一个仿真也可以以受限访问方式运行，如在真实机器人上那样，或以特权访问方式运行以获取其完整状态（§ 2.1），因此它可同时服务于评估、特权实验和训练。 附录 D 提供了更多细节。

paragraphs.en: Each simulation runs as a server, and a policy connects to it over an authenticated HTTP API, whose key grants restricted or privileged access (§ 2.1 ). To support policies ranging from frontier models to code policies and VLAs, a policy can command the robot at several levels. It can set joint targets or end-effector coordinates, which a controller tracks, or send joint torques and, on humanoids, individual motor commands. Like a computer-use agent, it can also press game-style keys, such as W, A, S, and D to move the end effector, each held for a set number of control ticks.
paragraphs.zh: 每个仿真作为服务器运行，策略通过经过身份验证的 HTTP API 连接到它，其密钥授予受限或特权访问权限（§ 2.1）。 为了支持从前沿模型到代码策略和 VLA 的各种策略，策略可以在多个层级上指挥机器人。 它可以设置关节目标或末端执行器坐标（由控制器进行跟踪），也可以发送关节力矩，以及在人形机器人上发送单独的电机指令。 类似计算机使用智能体，它还可以按下游戏风格的按键（例如 W、A、S 和 D）来移动末端执行器，每次按键保持设定的控制节拍数。

paragraphs.en: Each attempt runs on an independent copy of the simulation, starting from the task’s initial state, with a wall-clock budget of three hours. paragraphs.zh: 每次尝试都在模拟的一个独立副本上运行，从任务的初始状态开始，墙钟时间预算为三小时。 智能体完成后，验证器对每次尝试进行评分。 在尝试过程中，智能体不会观察到奖励。 我们报告两个指标：(1) 成功率，即验证器判定为成功的尝试所占的比例；(2) 平均奖励，即连续奖励 r ∈ [ 0 , 1 ] r\in[0,1] 的均值，该奖励反映部分进展程度。

paragraphs.en: Figure 6 shows the performance of three frontier models on RoboWorld. None of them completes any of the 25 test tasks, so all three achieve a success rate of 0%. Their average rewards of only 0.002 to 0.06 show that they make little progress within these tasks, and even the strongest model, Claude Opus 5.5, earns no reward at all on 16 of the 25 tasks. On an easier subset of 25 tasks from the training split, all three models complete some tasks, and Claude Opus 5.5 is again the strongest, with a success rate of 32% and an average reward of 0.48, followed by GPT-6 Astra (24%, 0.41) and GPT-6.1 Terra (12%, 0.17). These results highlight that, while frontier models can complete some simpler tasks, they remain far from performing realistic physical work, establishing RoboWorld as a challenging benchmark for embodied AI. Moreover, since at least one model completes 44% of the easier tasks, and the models earn partial reward on most of the rest, these tasks are in the sweet spot of difficulty for training frontier models with reinforcement learning.
paragraphs.zh: 图6展示了三个前沿模型在RoboWorld上的表现。 它们没有完成25个测试任务中的任何一个，因此三者的成功率均为0%。 它们仅有0.002到0.06的平均奖励表明它们在这些任务中几乎没有取得进展，即使是最强的模型Claude Opus 5.5，在25个任务中也有16个完全没有获得奖励。 在来自训练集的一个由25个较简单任务组成的子集上，三个模型都完成了一些任务，Claude Opus 5.5再次表现最强，成功率为32%，平均奖励为0.48，其次是GPT-6 Astra（24%，0.41）和GPT-6.1 Terra（12%，0.17）。 这些结果凸显出，尽管前沿模型能够完成一些较简单的任务，但它们距离执行现实的物理工作仍然很远，从而使RoboWorld成为具身AI的一个具有挑战性的基准。 此外，由于至少有一个模型完成了44%的较简单任务，并且模型在其余大多数任务上获得了部分奖励，这些任务恰好处于使用强化学习训练前沿模型的难度最佳区间。

paragraphs.en: We group the 25 easier tasks into three levels by the degrees of freedom (DoF) of their robot. Fixed-base arms (17 tasks) have 8 to 16 DoF, and are mostly two Franka FR3 arms with parallel grippers. The mobile manipulator (5 tasks) is the Franka Mobile FR3 Duo, which adds a moving base and a lift to two FR3 arms, for 20 DoF. The humanoids (3 tasks) are the Unitree G1 with Dex3 hands and the Unitree H1-2 with Inspire hands, with 43 and 39 DoF. Table 3 shows the results at each level. With fixed-base arms, the models succeed on 18 to 35% of tasks. With the mobile manipulator, each model succeeds on at most 20% of tasks. With humanoids, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra earn no reward at all, and Claude Opus 5.5 succeeds only in football, by kicking the ball while the robot falls (§ 6.3 ). paragraphs.en: We found very intriguing behaviors of frontier models as they attempt RoboWorld tasks (Figure 8 ). For instance, in football, Claude Opus 5.5 had to kick a ball into a goal with a humanoid. It built its own simulation of the robot, found that the robot could not stay standing, and therefore designed a kick that strikes the ball while the robot falls. It scored without ever seeing the goal. Similarly, in percussion, where the robot plays a xylophone, it turned the simulated microphone into a sensor, using sound to detect when the mallet touched a bar and which note it played. When a note came out wrong, it worked out that the mallet had twisted in its gripper. GPT-6 Astra also brought tools and knowledge from the real world into our simulations. When driving a forklift, it found the brake by reading the operator manual of a real Toyota forklift. In the whiteboard task, it ran a pretrained get-up policy on its fallen humanoid, and since the robot has no tilt sensor, it estimated the robot’s tilt from the ceiling lines in its camera. However, frontier models also often overstate their success and even try to game the verifier. For example, GPT-6 Astra reported that the brake had stopped the forklift, while the forklift had in fact reversed into a wall. In filleting, where the fish frame must end up in a pan separate from the fillets, Claude Opus 5.5 expected the verifier to check only the frame, and placed the whole uncut fish in that pan, hoping for partial credit. Since our verifier measures the physical state of the simulation (§ 4 ), it found the fillet meat in the pan and gave no reward.

Since the two settings differ only in access to the simulator state, this gap shows that the ground-truth state of a simulation is a strong learning signal.
paragraphs.zh: 在受限访问条件下，Opus 5.5 在多次尝试中稳步提升，从 0.14 提升到 0.22，相对提升 54%，且没有任何权重更新。 在特权访问条件下，Opus 5.5 提升得明显更快：其第一次尝试就达到 0.34，超过了受限智能体三次尝试后的表现，其第三次尝试则达到 0.41。 例如，在足球和焊接任务上，特权智能体从第一次尝试起就获得了满分奖励，而受限智能体即使经过三次尝试也未能在任一任务上获得满分奖励。 由于这两种设置的唯一区别在于能否访问模拟器状态，这一差距表明模拟的真实状态（ground-truth state）是一种很强的学习信号。

paragraphs.en: Since privileged state is unavailable outside simulation, we next examine whether its benefits can be passed to a model that lacks it. Remarkably, the coached student, which never observes the privileged state and receives only qualitative hints, achieves 0.29 on its first attempt, a 2.1 × \times improvement over the solo agent and higher than the solo agent after all three attempts. This recovers 75% of the gap between the solo and privileged agents from the very first attempt. On football and welding, the coached student achieves full reward on every attempt, matching its teacher. We attribute these gains to the design of the coach: before each hint, it reads the true state of the student’s simulation, and can therefore point out mistakes that the student cannot observe directly. A single hint can also change the student’s whole strategy. For instance, in towel folding, GPT-6 Astra failed for over four hours to hold the towel with both grippers at once. Its coach, which had attempted the task with privileged access, read the student’s privileged state and suggested folding in stages with one gripper, so that the table supports most of the fabric. The student switched to this strategy and succeeded about 40 minutes later (Appendix F ). Overall, these results show that a frontier model with privileged state in simulation can teach a model that sees only what a real robot sees.

paragraphs.en: We test this on two tasks in a gift box simulation with two FR3 arms: removing the lid and placing it on the table without disturbing the box, and opening the box to move a named block into a tray. Code policies written with privileged access succeed on 96.7% of 2,048 varied initial states, 99.8% for lid removal and 93.7% for block retrieval. We keep 1,000 successful rollouts, 500 per task, spread evenly across eight groups of physics variations, and train π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} on them. Although π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} observes only three camera views and robot proprioception, the trained policy raises success on these tasks from 0% to 53% (Figure 7 , right). It also keeps this success on variations that it never saw in training: with unseen object poses, appearance, and physics, it succeeds in 55% of attempts. Moreover, π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} matches the success rate of Claude Opus 5.5 controlling the robot step by step, and comes close in average reward, 0.87 against 0.93. It also completes a task in about two minutes, 14 times faster than Claude Opus 5.5, which takes about 29 minutes. This shows that, with simulation, a frontier model can write code policies that produce thousands of demonstrations, which can train a small, fast policy such as π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} that can in principle be deployed on a real robot.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在包含两条 FR3 机械臂的礼品盒仿真中，在两个任务上测试这一点：在不碰到盒子的前提下取下盖子并放到桌上，以及打开盒子将指定名称的方块移动到托盘中。 以特权访问方式编写的代码策略在 2,048 个不同的初始状态上成功率达 96.7%，其中取盖任务为 99.8%，方块取回任务为 93.7%。 我们保留 1,000 条成功的回放数据，每个任务 500 条，均匀分布在八组物理变化之中，并用它们训练 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5}。 尽管 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 只观测三个相机视角和机器人本体感知，训练后的策略将这些任务的成功率从 0% 提升到 53%（图 7，右）。 它在训练中从未见过的变化上仍保持这一成功率：在物体位姿、外观和物理属性均未见过的情况下，其尝试成功率为 55%。 此外，π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 的成功率与逐步控制机器人的 Claude Opus 5.5 相当，平均奖励也接近，为 0.87 对 0.93。 它完成一个任务约需两分钟，比约需 29 分钟的 Claude Opus 5.5 快 14 倍。 这表明，借助仿真，前沿模型可以编写出能产生数千条演示的代码策略，这些演示可以训练出像 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 这样小而快的策略，后者原则上可以部署在真实机器人上。

sents.en: We test this on two tasks in a gift box simulation with two FR3 arms: removing the lid and placing it on the table without disturbing the box, and opening the box to move a named block into a tray.

sents.en: Code policies written with privileged access succeed on 96.7% of 2,048 varied initial states, 99.8% for lid removal and 93.7% for block retrieval.
sents.zh: 以特权访问方式编写的代码策略在 2,048 个不同的初始状态上成功率达 96.7%，其中取盖任务为 99.8%，方块取回任务为 93.7%。

sents.en: We keep 1,000 successful rollouts, 500 per task, spread evenly across eight groups of physics variations, and train π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} on them.
sents.zh: 我们保留 1,000 条成功的回放数据，每个任务 500 条，均匀分布在八组物理变化之中，并用它们训练 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5}。

sents.en: Although π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} observes only three camera views and robot proprioception, the trained policy raises success on these tasks from 0% to 53% (Figure 7 , right).
sents.zh: 尽管 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 只观测三个相机视角和机器人本体感知，训练后的策略将这些任务的成功率从 0% 提升到 53%（图 7，右）。

sents.en: It also keeps this success on variations that it never saw in training: with unseen object poses, appearance, and physics, it succeeds in 55% of attempts.
sents.zh: 它在训练中从未见过的变化上仍保持这一成功率：在物体位姿、外观和物理属性均未见过的情况下，其尝试成功率为 55%。

sents.en: Moreover, π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} matches the success rate of Claude Opus 5.5 controlling the robot step by step, and comes close in average reward, 0.87 against 0.93.
sents.zh: 此外，π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 的成功率与逐步控制机器人的 Claude Opus 5.5 相当，平均奖励也接近，为 0.87 对 0.93。

sents.en: It also completes a task in about two minutes, 14 times faster than Claude Opus 5.5, which takes about 29 minutes.
sents.zh: 它完成一个任务约需两分钟，比约需 29 分钟的 Claude Opus 5.5 快 14 倍。

sents.en: This shows that, with simulation, a frontier model can write code policies that produce thousands of demonstrations, which can train a small, fast policy such as π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} that can in principle be deployed on a real robot.
sents.zh: 这表明，借助仿真，前沿模型可以编写出能产生数千条演示的代码策略，这些演示可以训练出像 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 这样小而快的策略，后者原则上可以部署在真实机器人上。

paragraphs.en: For each of our 25 simulations, research agents searched the web for prior simulators of the same core physical interaction, such as liquid pouring or cloth folding, and selected the strongest one with public code and a paper, ranked mainly by the physical accuracy of its solver and fixed before any comparison was run. Claude Opus 5.5 then compared each pair blind, with the two simulators labeled only A and B and their order swapped across two runs, using a prompt separate from the audit prompts that guided our simulations, so that the comparison does not favor our own criteria. Our simulations lose to the prior simulator in only 14% of comparisons on visuals and 24% on physics, and win 80% and 76%, respectively (Figure 9 ).
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的 25 个仿真中，每一个都由研究智能体在网上搜索针对同一核心物理交互（例如倒液体或叠布料）的先前仿真器，并选出其中最强的一个，要求其具有公开代码和论文，排名主要依据其求解器的物理精度，并在任何对比运行之前就固定下来。 随后，Claude Opus 5.5 以盲评方式对每一对进行对比，两个仿真器仅被标记为 A 和 B，且其顺序在两次运行中互换；对比所用的提示词与引导我们仿真的审计提示词相互独立，从而使对比不会偏向我们自己的标准。 我们的仿真仅在 14% 的对比中在外观上输给先前仿真器，在 24% 的对比中在物理上落败，而分别以 80% 和 76% 的比例获胜（图 9）。

paragraphs.en: We attribute the realism of our simulations to the creation-audit loop (§ 3 ). When auditors found a physics error, it was typically in the first round. For instance, in welding, the physics engine moved a loose bracket, while the heat model and the renderer kept a copy of it at its starting pose, so the arc welded a bracket that was no longer there. In ingredient mixing, a tilted pan lost most of its sauce through its steel wall before the sauce could reach the rim. The creation agent fixed both errors in the next round.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将仿真结果的真实感归因于创建—审计循环（§ 3 ）。 当审计员发现物理错误时，该错误通常出现在第一轮。 例如，在焊接场景中，物理引擎移动了一个松动的支架，而热模型和渲染器仍保留着它起始位姿的副本，于是电弧焊的是一个已经不存在的支架。 在食材混合场景中，一口倾斜的平底锅让大部分酱汁在到达锅沿之前就从钢制锅壁漏了出去。 创建智能体在下一轮修复了这两处错误。

paragraphs.en: The adversarial audit agent (§ 3 ) tries to break each simulation using only legal robot actions, and it found a real defect in about three quarters of our simulations. For instance, in football, pushing the ball into the turf made the turf model launch it out at high speed without any robot contact. In ingredient mixing, lowering the bowl past the edge of the counter left the sauce floating at counter height. The creation agent repaired these defects in the next round and verified each repair by replaying the audit’s own reproduction.
paragraphs.zh: 对抗性审计智能体（第 3 节）试图仅使用合法的机器人动作来破坏每个仿真，它在约四分之三的仿真中发现了真实缺陷。 例如，在足球任务中，把球压进球场草皮会使草皮模型让球以高速弹射出去，而没有任何机器人接触。 在食材搅拌任务中，把碗放低超过台面边缘后，酱汁会悬浮在台面高度。 创建智能体在下一轮修复了这些缺陷，并通过重放审计智能体自身的复现步骤来验证每一项修复。

paragraphs.en: The task audits (§ 4 ) test each verifier on constructed states, such as an untouched scene or a partly finished task. They often found several issues in a verifier. For instance, in barcode scanning, most checks only tested that nothing had gone wrong, so an untouched shelf scored higher than a partly scanned one. In football, the verifier ruled genuine goals just inside a post as misses, so these episodes could never succeed. These audits ensured that rewards are progressive, i.e., that more progress earns more credit, which is important for training with RL.
paragraphs.zh: 任务审计（§ 4）在构造的状态上测试每个验证器，例如完全未动的场景或部分完成的任务。 他们通常在每个验证器中发现了若干问题。 例如，在条形码扫描中，大多数检查只测试是否没有出错，因此完全未动的货架得分高于部分扫描的货架。 在足球中，验证器将真正射入门柱内侧的进球判定为未命中，因此这些片段永远无法成功。 这些审计确保奖励是渐进的，即更多的进展获得更多的积分，这对使用强化学习进行训练非常重要。

paragraphs.en: Fast physics engines ( Todorov et al., 2012 ; Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ; Tao et al., 2025 ; Genesis Authors, 2024 ) support many robotics benchmarks, but these benchmarks are built mostly by hand and therefore cover a narrow slice of physical work (Table 2 ). Most target rigid and articulated objects in tabletop, household, or workplace scenes ( Yu et al., 2020 ; James et al., 2020 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2021 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ; Nasiriany et al., 2026 ; Lan et al., 2026 ; Gajo et al., 2025 ) , while others target a single class of deformable materials, such as liquids ( Xian et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2025b ; Gong et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2025a ) , cloth ( Seita et al., 2021 ; Lu et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Hu et al., 2025 ) , or plasticine ( Huang et al., 2021 ; Lin et al., 2022 ) , and only a few combine several ( Lin et al., 2020 ; Gu et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023 ; Li et al., 2026 ) . BEHAVIOR-1K ( Li et al., 2023 ) comes closest to broad coverage, with liquids, cloth, and activities from time-use surveys. In contrast, RoboWorld is built by coding agents, which implement physics that existing engines lack, and its simulations are selected by the economic value of physical work.
paragraphs.zh: 快速物理引擎（Todorov 等，2012；Makoviychuk 等，2021；Tao 等，2025；Genesis Authors，2024）支持许多机器人学基准，但这些基准大多由人工构建，因此仅覆盖物理工作的狭窄一隅（表 2）。 大多数基准针对桌面、家庭或工作场所场景中的刚体和铰接物体（Yu 等，2020；James 等，2020；Liu 等，2023；Li 等，2021；Nasiriany 等，2024；Nasiriany 等，2026；Lan 等，2026；Gajo 等，2025），另一些则针对单一类别的可变形材料，例如液体（Xian 等，2023；Li 等，2025b；Gong 等，2023；Li 等，2025a）、布料（Seita 等，2021；Lu 等，2024；Wang 等，2025b；Hu 等，2025）或黏土（Huang 等，2021；Lin 等，2022），只有少数基准结合了多种材料（Lin 等，2020；Gu 等，2023；Chen 等，2023；Li 等，2026）。 BEHAVIOR-1K（Li 等，2023）最接近广泛覆盖，包含液体、布料以及来自时间使用调查的活动。 相比之下，RoboWorld 由智能体编写代码构建，这些智能体实现了现有引擎所缺乏的物理特性，并且其仿真依据物理工作的经济价值进行遴选。

paragraphs.en: Prior work makes simulated physics more faithful through system identification ( Tan et al., 2018 ) , randomization ( Tobin et al., 2017 ; Peng et al., 2018 ) , real-to-sim reconstruction ( Torne et al., 2024 ) , and specialized solvers ( Xian et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024b ; Heiden et al., 2021 ) , and recent benchmarks measure the sim-to-real gap directly for cloth ( Blanco-Mulero et al., 2024 ; Hu et al., 2025 ) , but each of these requires experts to model the physics of a single task or material. LLM-based generators instead scale simulation creation by writing task code, demonstration programs, scenes, or rewards ( Wang et al., 2024a ; Hua et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2024b ; Wang et al., 2024c ; Ma et al., 2024 ) , but they build on the fixed physics of an existing engine and check their output through policy success or visual inspection rather than physical measurements. Building on the creation-audit loop of Gym-Anything ( Aggarwal et al., 2026 ) , our coding agents implement the physics itself, and audit agents check it through physical measurements, assisted demonstrations, and adversarial robot actions.
paragraphs.zh: 已有工作通过系统辨识（Tan 等，2018）、随机化（Tobin 等，2017；Peng 等，2018）、实到仿真重建（Torne 等，2024）以及专用求解器（Xian 等，2023；Wang 等，2024b；Heiden 等，2021）使模拟物理更加逼真，最近的基准测试则直接针对布料测量仿真到现实（sim-to-real）的差距（Blanco-Mulero 等，2024；Hu 等，2025），但这些方法都需要专家为单一任务或材料手动建模物理。 基于 LLM 的生成器则通过编写任务代码、示教程序、场景或奖励来扩展仿真创建的规模（Wang 等，2024a；Hua 等，2024；Chen 等，2026；Yang 等，2024b；Wang 等，2024c；Ma 等，2024），但它们建立在现有引擎的固定物理之上，并且通过策略成功率或视觉检查而非物理测量来检验其输出。 基于 Gym-Anything 的创建-审计循环（Aggarwal 等，2026），我们的编码智能体实现物理本身，而审计智能体则通过物理测量、辅助示教和对抗性机器人动作来对其进行检验。

paragraphs.en: Frontier models act in simulated and physical worlds by writing code ( Liang et al., 2023 ; Huang et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023 ) or by controlling robots directly ( Gemini Robotics Team, 2025 ) , are evaluated as embodied agents ( Yang et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) , and improve from repeated attempts in context ( Brown et al., 2020 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) . Separately, robot learning uses the privileged state of simulators to train students from privileged teachers ( Chen et al., 2020 ; Lee et al., 2020 ; Pinto et al., 2018 ) and to generate demonstrations at scale ( Mandlekar et al., 2023 ; Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) , but these teachers pass their knowledge to students through weight updates. We bring the two lines together, showing that privileged state helps frontier models learn in context, reaches a student through qualitative hints alone or through the model’s own privileged experience, and trains VLAs through privileged code policies. paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduced Gym-Anything for Robotics, a scalable framework in which coding agents build realistic robotics simulations. By framing simulation creation as a coding agent task and checking each simulation and task in a multi-agent loop of creation, auditing, and repair, Gym-Anything for Robotics addresses a central bottleneck in robot learning: the difficulty of building realistic simulations at scale. Applying this framework, we built RoboWorld, a GDP-grounded collection of 200 RL environments across 25 simulations spanning liquids, cloth, and physics that existing engines lack, with swappable robots and train and test splits. We further showed that privileged simulator state more than doubles the first-attempt reward of frontier models, and that it can teach a student through hints alone and train π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} from 0% to 53% success. At the same time, RoboWorld is challenging even for frontier models, which fail every test task, indicating that realistic physical work remains far from solved.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出了 Gym-Anything for Robotics，这是一个可扩展的框架，由编码智能体构建逼真的机器人学仿真。 通过将仿真创建设定为编码智能体任务，并在创建、审计、修复的多智能体循环中检查每个仿真和任务，Gym-Anything for Robotics 解决了机器人学习中的一个核心瓶颈：难以大规模构建逼真的仿真。 应用该框架，我们构建了 RoboWorld，这是一个以 GDP 为基础的集合，包含 25 个仿真中的 200 个强化学习环境，涵盖现有引擎所缺乏的液体、布料和物理效果，并支持可更换的机器人以及训练与测试划分。 我们进一步表明，特权仿真器状态使前沿模型首次尝试的奖励翻了一倍以上，并且它可以仅通过提示教会一个学生模型，并将 π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} 的成功率从 0% 训练到 53%。 与此同时，RoboWorld 即使对前沿模型也极具挑战性，它们在所有测试任务上都失败了，这表明逼真的物理工作仍远未解决。

paragraphs.en: For paid work, we use the O*NET database, which describes 1,016 occupations through 18,796 task statements, each rated for importance and frequency [ Peterson et al., 2001 ] . Similar to prior work [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] , we estimate the economic value of each occupation as its wage bill (employment × \times mean wage) from Bureau of Labor Statistics data [ U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025b ] , scaled to national accounts data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis [ U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, 2025 ] . We then distribute each occupation’s value across its tasks in proportion to their importance and frequency ratings. However, paid work misses much of what people physically do, such as cooking, cleaning, and caring for others. For everyday life, we therefore use the American Time Use Survey (ATUS), which estimates the time the U.S. population spends on each of 465 activities [ U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025a ] . We keep the two streams separate throughout, since dollars and population-hours measure different quantities and combining them would require an arbitrary exchange rate.

paragraphs.en: The creation agent receives the complete record of an action group, including all of its action variants, required capabilities, and grounding, rather than only its name. It then works in two phases within the same session. In the first phase, research and design, the agent reads every action and capability in the group and researches how the activity is performed: its real setting, objects, equipment, dimensions, materials, mechanisms, and the robot typically used, using primary documentation, published research, and other digital evidence. It then designs a concrete scenario that exercises the capabilities of the action group, and works through the equations, numerical implementation, and engine support the scenario requires before running expensive experiments. In the second phase, the agent builds, demonstrates, and documents the simulation. It assembles the scene from real assets, typically combining a photorealistic Gaussian-splat backdrop [ Kerbl et al., 2023 ] , which carries no physics, with explicit physical bodies for every object the robot can touch. It implements the task-relevant physics, including physics the engine does not provide, integrates a default robot from the shared catalog, and defines tasks. Crucially, every change in the world must be physically caused by the robot: missing mechanics may not be replaced by animations, attachments, or scripted outcomes. The agent then collects evidence, including videos, physical measurements, and assisted demonstrations, and writes a report covering the scenario, sources, equations, parameter choices, experiments, and limitations. We send the build prompt only after the research phase finishes, without announcing it earlier, so that the agent researches diligently instead of hurrying to build.
paragraphs.zh: 创建智能体接收动作组的完整记录，包括其所有动作变体、所需能力和落地依据，而不仅仅是其名称。 然后，它在同一会话中分两个阶段工作。 在第一阶段，即研究与设计阶段，智能体阅读组中的每个动作和能力，并研究该活动是如何进行的：其真实场景、物体、设备、维度、材料、机制以及通常使用的机器人，依据是原始文档、已发表的研究和其他数字证据。 然后，它设计一个能锻炼该动作组各项能力的具体场景，并在运行高成本实验之前，先梳理该场景所需的方程、数值实现和引擎支持。 在第二阶段，智能体构建、演示并记录该仿真。 它用真实资产搭建场景，通常将不携带物理属性的照片级高斯泼溅背景 [ Kerbl et al., 2023 ] 与机器人可接触的每个物体的显式物理刚体相结合。 它实现与任务相关的物理，包括引擎不提供的物理，从共享目录中集成一个默认机器人，并定义任务。 至关重要的是，世界中的每一个变化都必须由机器人物理地引发：缺失的机制不得用动画、附着物或脚本化的结果来替代。 随后，智能体收集证据，包括视频、物理测量和辅助演示，并撰写一份报告，涵盖场景、来源、方程、参数选择、实验和局限性。 我们只在与研究阶段完成之后才发送构建提示，且不提前告知，以便智能体认真开展研究，而不是急于构建。

paragraphs.en: Each of the four audit agents checks one category of criteria from § 3 . In each round, fresh audit agents examine the current simulation and write reports, which are returned to the same creation agent to repair the code, scene, and evidence. The audit agent for dynamics and solvability judges the dynamics from the videos and scripts of the creation agent, and from its own runs of the simulation, assisted by a video model. The audit agent for speed and configuration requires that a simulation run at most 200 times slower than real time. The audit agent for robustness reads the code and searches for legal robot actions that produce non-finite values, energy blow-ups, or physically impossible motion, and returns its evidence to the creation agent. The written audits further let us independently verify the quality of each simulation.

For instance, a barcode label counts as applied only if the barcode is decoded from a rendered camera image. In practice, the auditor found that the verifiers of a labeling simulation rejected otherwise valid completions in which the part had moved by 60 mm, because of a 50 mm displacement limit that the task never stated.
paragraphs.zh: 在可能的情况下，验证器测量定义完成的物理机制或传感器信号，而不是仅测量物体位姿。 例如，只有当条形码能从渲染的相机图像中被解码时，该条形码标签才算作已贴附。 在实践中，审计员发现某贴标仿真的验证器会拒绝原本有效的完成情况，即零件移动了 60 mm 的情况，原因是存在一个任务从未说明的 50 mm 位移限制。

paragraphs.en: Similar to prior work [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] , the library separates three parts: the core runtime, simulation packages, and agents. The core provides the registry of simulations, session management, authentication, decoding of robot commands, recording, a command-line interface, and a browser dashboard. Each simulation package contains its scene, robots, physics, sensing, task definitions, verifiers, and scene variations. Agents are independent clients, either Python plugins or separate processes that connect over HTTP, so an agent can be replaced without changing any simulation. The Python API, the command-line interface, and the HTTP API all construct simulations through the same registry.
paragraphs.zh: 与先前的工作 [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] 类似，该库分为三个部分：核心运行时、仿真包和智能体。 核心提供仿真的注册表、会话管理、身份验证、机器人指令解码、录制、命令行界面和浏览器仪表板。 每个仿真包包含其场景、机器人、物理、感知、任务定义、验证器和场景变体。 智能体是独立的客户端，可以是 Python 插件，也可以是通过 HTTP 连接的独立进程，因此可以在不更改任何仿真的情况下替换智能体。 Python API、命令行界面和 HTTP API 都通过同一个注册表构建仿真。

paragraphs.en: Every policy, from a frontier model to a VLA, controls the robot through the same set of commands (Table 4 ). paragraphs.en: Simulation has long been a central tool for robot learning, and physics engines such as MuJoCo [ Todorov et al., 2012 ] , Isaac Gym [ Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ] , ManiSkill3 [ Tao et al., 2025 ] , and Genesis [ Genesis Authors, 2024 ] make it fast, with GPU-parallel engines running thousands of environments at once. Benchmarks built on these engines cover tabletop manipulation of rigid and articulated objects [ Yu et al., 2020 , James et al., 2020 , Liu et al., 2023 ] , household environments [ Li et al., 2021 , Nasiriany et al., 2024 , Nasiriany et al., 2026 ] , and specific workplaces such as laboratories [ Li et al., 2025a , Lan et al., 2026 ] and retail stores [ Gajo et al., 2025 ] . A separate line of benchmarks targets deformable materials, such as liquids [ Xian et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2025b , Gong et al., 2023 ] , cloth and garments [ Seita et al., 2021 , Lu et al., 2024 , Wang et al., 2025b , Hu et al., 2025 ] , plasticine [ Huang et al., 2021 , Lin et al., 2022 ] , or several of these [ Lin et al., 2020 , Gu et al., 2023 , Chen et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2026 ] . BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] comes closest to broad coverage, simulating both liquids and cloth and grounding its 1,000 household activities in time-use surveys. However, these benchmarks are built mostly by hand, so each covers only the materials and activities that its authors chose and could implement, and adding a new kind of physics requires substantial expert effort. Moreover, none of the benchmarks in Table 2 selects its tasks or simulations by the economic value of physical work, and only RGBench [ Hu et al., 2025 ] , which targets garments, checks its simulated physics against real measurements. In contrast, Gym-Anything for Robotics uses coding agents to build each simulation, including physics that existing engines lack, selects simulations based on occupation and time-use data, and checks the physics of each simulation against physical theory and, where available, real measurements.
paragraphs.zh: 仿真长期以来一直是机器人学习的核心工具，而诸如 MuJoCo [ Todorov et al., 2012 ]、Isaac Gym [ Makoviychuk et al., 2021 ]、ManiSkill3 [ Tao et al., 2025 ] 和 Genesis [ Genesis Authors, 2024 ] 这样的物理引擎使其变得快速，GPU 并行引擎可以同时运行数千个环境。 基于这些引擎构建的基准测试涵盖了刚体和铰接物体的桌面操作 [ Yu et al., 2020 , James et al., 2020 , Liu et al., 2023 ]、家庭环境 [ Li et al., 2021 , Nasiriany et al., 2024 , Nasiriany et al., 2026 ]，以及实验室 [ Li et al., 2025a , Lan et al., 2026 ] 和零售店 [ Gajo et al., 2025 ] 等特定工作场所。 另一系列基准测试则针对可变形材料，例如液体 [ Xian et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2025b , Gong et al., 2023 ]、布料和衣物 [ Seita et al., 2021 , Lu et al., 2024 , Wang et al., 2025b , Hu et al., 2025 ]、橡皮泥 [ Huang et al., 2021 , Lin et al., 2022 ]，或上述多种材料的组合 [ Lin et al., 2020 , Gu et al., 2023 , Chen et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2026 ]。 BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] 在覆盖面上最为广泛，它同时仿真液体和布料，并基于时间使用调查将其 1,000 项家庭活动落到实处。 然而，这些基准测试大多是手工构建的，因此每个基准只涵盖其作者选择并能够实现的那部分材料和活动，而添加一种新的物理类型需要大量的专家投入。 此外，表 2 中的基准测试没有一个根据体力劳动的经济价值来选择任务或仿真，只有面向衣物的 RGBench [ Hu et al., 2025 ] 对照真实测量结果检验了其仿真物理。 相比之下，Gym-Anything for Robotics 使用编码智能体来构建每个仿真，包括现有引擎所缺乏的物理，基于职业和时间使用数据选择仿真，并依据物理理论以及（在可行的情况下）真实测量结果来检验每个仿真的物理。

sents.en: Benchmarks built on these engines cover tabletop manipulation of rigid and articulated objects [ Yu et al., 2020 , James et al., 2020 , Liu et al., 2023 ] , household environments [ Li et al., 2021 , Nasiriany et al., 2024 , Nasiriany et al., 2026 ] , and specific workplaces such as laboratories [ Li et al., 2025a , Lan et al., 2026 ] and retail stores [ Gajo et al., 2025 ] .
sents.zh: 基于这些引擎构建的基准测试涵盖了刚体和铰接物体的桌面操作 [ Yu et al., 2020 , James et al., 2020 , Liu et al., 2023 ]、家庭环境 [ Li et al., 2021 , Nasiriany et al., 2024 , Nasiriany et al., 2026 ]，以及实验室 [ Li et al., 2025a , Lan et al., 2026 ] 和零售店 [ Gajo et al., 2025 ] 等特定工作场所。

sents.en: A separate line of benchmarks targets deformable materials, such as liquids [ Xian et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2025b , Gong et al., 2023 ] , cloth and garments [ Seita et al., 2021 , Lu et al., 2024 , Wang et al., 2025b , Hu et al., 2025 ] , plasticine [ Huang et al., 2021 , Lin et al., 2022 ] , or several of these [ Lin et al., 2020 , Gu et al., 2023 , Chen et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2026 ] .
sents.zh: 另一系列基准测试则针对可变形材料，例如液体 [ Xian et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2025b , Gong et al., 2023 ]、布料和衣物 [ Seita et al., 2021 , Lu et al., 2024 , Wang et al., 2025b , Hu et al., 2025 ]、橡皮泥 [ Huang et al., 2021 , Lin et al., 2022 ]，或上述多种材料的组合 [ Lin et al., 2020 , Gu et al., 2023 , Chen et al., 2023 , Li et al., 2026 ]。

sents.en: BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] comes closest to broad coverage, simulating both liquids and cloth and grounding its 1,000 household activities in time-use surveys.
sents.zh: BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] 在覆盖面上最为广泛，它同时仿真液体和布料，并基于时间使用调查将其 1,000 项家庭活动落到实处。

sents.en: However, these benchmarks are built mostly by hand, so each covers only the materials and activities that its authors chose and could implement, and adding a new kind of physics requires substantial expert effort.
sents.zh: 然而，这些基准测试大多是手工构建的，因此每个基准只涵盖其作者选择并能够实现的那部分材料和活动，而添加一种新的物理类型需要大量的专家投入。

sents.en: Moreover, none of the benchmarks in Table 2 selects its tasks or simulations by the economic value of physical work, and only RGBench [ Hu et al., 2025 ] , which targets garments, checks its simulated physics against real measurements.
sents.zh: 此外，表 2 中的基准测试没有一个根据体力劳动的经济价值来选择任务或仿真，只有面向衣物的 RGBench [ Hu et al., 2025 ] 对照真实测量结果检验了其仿真物理。

sents.en: In contrast, Gym-Anything for Robotics uses coding agents to build each simulation, including physics that existing engines lack, selects simulations based on occupation and time-use data, and checks the physics of each simulation against physical theory and, where available, real measurements.
sents.zh: 相比之下，Gym-Anything for Robotics 使用编码智能体来构建每个仿真，包括现有引擎所缺乏的物理，基于职业和时间使用数据选择仿真，并依据物理理论以及（在可行的情况下）真实测量结果来检验每个仿真的物理。

paragraphs.en: Whether simulated physics can be trusted is a long-standing question in robotics, since policies trained in simulation degrade when its physics differs from the real world. A large body of work narrows this sim-to-real gap by identifying physical parameters from real data [ Tan et al., 2018 ] , randomizing them during training [ Tobin et al., 2017 , Peng et al., 2018 ] , or reconstructing real scenes in simulation [ Torne et al., 2024 ] , while specialized solvers model materials that general-purpose engines handle poorly, such as liquids [ Xian et al., 2023 ] , thin shells [ Wang et al., 2024b ] , and cutting [ Heiden et al., 2021 ] . These methods can produce faithful physics for a specific task, but each requires experts to model and tune the physics by hand. Recent benchmarks also measure this gap directly, by comparing simulated cloth with real cloth manipulated by robots [ Blanco-Mulero et al., 2024 , Hu et al., 2025 ] , but they cover a single material. A more recent line of work uses LLMs to generate simulations, writing task code [ Wang et al., 2024a , Hua et al., 2024 ] , demonstration programs [ Chen et al., 2026 ] , scenes [ Yang et al., 2024b , Wang et al., 2024c ] , or reward functions [ Ma et al., 2024 ] . However, these methods generate tasks and scenes on top of the fixed physics of an existing engine, which largely limits them to rigid and articulated objects, and they check their output through policy success, visual inspection, or human review rather than by measuring the simulated physics. Our work builds on the creation-audit loop of Gym-Anything [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] , which verifies environments built from real software, and extends it to physics, where coding agents implement the physics itself and audit agents check it through physical measurements, assisted demonstrations, and adversarial robot actions.

paragraphs.en: Frontier models increasingly act in simulated and physical worlds, either by writing programs that call perception and control primitives [ Liang et al., 2023 , Huang et al., 2023 ] or by controlling robots directly [ Gemini Robotics Team, 2025 ] , and several benchmarks evaluate multimodal models as embodied agents [ Yang et al., 2025 , Zhang et al., 2024 ] . Such models can also improve without weight updates, by learning from repeated attempts in context [ Brown et al., 2020 , Shinn et al., 2023 ] or by building a library of skills as code, as Voyager [ Wang et al., 2023 ] does in Minecraft. Separately, robot learning has long used the privileged state of simulators, both by training a teacher with access to the true state and distilling it into a student that observes only sensors [ Chen et al., 2020 , Lee et al., 2020 , Pinto et al., 2018 ] , and by generating demonstrations in simulation at scale to train visuomotor policies [ Mandlekar et al., 2023 , Nasiriany et al., 2024 ] . However, these two lines of work rarely meet: privileged teachers pass their knowledge to students through weight updates, while frontier-model agents have been studied mainly in games and rigid-object scenes, without privileged state as a learning signal. We bring the two together on realistic simulations, showing that privileged state accelerates the in-context learning of frontier models, that a privileged frontier model can teach a student through qualitative hints alone, that a model can learn from its own privileged experience, and that privileged code policies can train VLAs that observe only cameras and proprioception.

paragraphs.en: A growing body of work connects AI capabilities to the economy through occupation data, most prominently by estimating which occupations and tasks in O*NET [ Peterson et al., 2001 ] are exposed to language models [ Eloundou et al., 2024 ] . These studies measure exposure rather than guide the design of benchmarks, but recent benchmarks have begun to use economic value directly: GDPval [ Patwardhan et al., 2025 ] evaluates models on tasks from 44 occupations across the nine sectors that contribute most to U.S. GDP, and Gym-Anything [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] selects software for computer-use environments by its attributed GDP. In robotics, BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] grounds its household activities in time-use surveys, but to our knowledge no prior robotics simulation benchmark draws on occupation data. Gym-Anything for Robotics extends GDP-grounded selection to physical work, combining the tasks and wages of each occupation with the time that people spend on everyday activities [ U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025a ] , and selects simulations that supply the physical capabilities that the most valuable actions require.
paragraphs.zh: 越来越多的工作通过职业数据将 AI 能力与经济联系起来，其中最突出的是估计 O*NET [ Peterson et al., 2001 ] 中哪些职业和任务会受到语言模型的影响 [ Eloundou et al., 2024 ] 。 这些研究衡量的是暴露程度而非指导基准的设计，但近期的基准已开始直接使用经济价值：GDPval [ Patwardhan et al., 2025 ] 在来自对美国 GDP 贡献最大的九个行业中 44 种职业的任务上评估模型， GDP，而 Gym-Anything [ Aggarwal et al., 2026 ] 则根据归因的 GDP 来为计算机使用环境选择软件。 在机器人领域，BEHAVIOR-1K [ Li et al., 2023 ] 将其家庭活动建立在时间使用调查之上，但据我们所知，此前没有机器人仿真基准利用职业数据。 Gym-Anything for Robotics 将基于 GDP 的选择扩展到体力工作，将每种职业的任务和工资与人们花费在日常活动上的时间相结合 [ U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 2025a ] ，并选择能够提供最有价值的行动所需的物理能力的仿真环境。
